From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@alcove.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, purchasing@alcove.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Usage spike during staging — help with reconciliation

Hi Avery,

Quick one — we noticed a significant usage spike on Feb 12–13 tied to our staging migration (we routed a few batch tests to prod accidentally). Our billing dashboard shows ~2.3M extra tokens and an associated one-off charge that will push us a material amount over our committed capacity for Q1.

Can Redwood help reconcile this and suggest options for a one-time adjustment or credit? We can pull the raw run logs but wanted to get a plan in motion while we gather them. Purchasing is looped to track any formal PO/invoice steps.

Thanks — we're hoping to avoid an unexpected invoice that derails the renewal conversation.

— Sofia Ramos
Director, Platform Engineering
Alcove Systems
sofia.ramos@alcove.com

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Usage spike during staging — help with reconciliation

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the heads-up and for looping purchasing. Sorry to hear it crept into production during migration — we see those happen more than we’d like. We can move fast here. To speed a clean reconciliation please:

- Share the exported usage file (start/end timestamps, request ids, token counts).
- Tell us which jobs/routes should be considered test traffic (we’ll treat them as eligible for a one-time wash if they meet the criteria).
- Confirm whether you want the resolution applied as a credit on the next invoice or as an adjusted invoice now.

Tentatively we can offer a partial one-time credit while our finance team runs the verification. I’ve looped Ben (billing lead) and Laura (account) to scope the amount and next steps.

I’ll follow up with Ben on a proposed settlement amount once we get the usage export.

Best,

Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Alcove usage export (Feb 1–14)

Hi all —

Attached is the export you requested: alcove_usage_report_q1.csv. Summary:
- Window: 2027-02-01 00:00 to 2027-02-14 23:59 (UTC)
- Total tokens billed: +4,812,300 for period; excess attributable to migration/test spike ~2,312,100 tokens
- Primary route: /api/v1/predict/staging-migration
- Notes: Our test harness inadvertently authenticates under our prod key when a particular flag is set. We’ve disabled the flag and added a safeguard.

We’re asking Redwood to consider:
1) Waiving or crediting the ~2.3M token excess as a one-time adjustment; or
2) If not fully eligible, apply a partial credit and simpler one-time top-up invoice we can pay immediately to settle the overage and proceed with renewal.

Let me know what you need from our side to verify.

Thanks — attaching the csv now.

— Sofia
(Attachment: alcove_usage_report_q1.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@alcove.com>
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, purchasing@alcove.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed settlement: Alcove Q1 staging spike

Sofia —

Thanks for the export, and for the clear notes on root cause. Finance reviewed Alcove’s usage and our proposed approach is below (aiming to be fair while respecting committed capacity).

Proposal (one-time):
- Gross overage charge calculated: $12,450 (covers the 2.3M token overage at your plan rates).
- Goodwill credit applied: $4,500 (we can apply this immediately as a credit toward the overage).
- Net one-time top-up due: $7,950.
- Operational concession: 90 days of free burst capacity (up to 500k tokens/month) to help with testing during your migration window.

We’ll issue an adjusted invoice (ALC-3342) for the net amount. If you prefer, we can apply the net as a credit against your next renewal invoice; otherwise we’ll generate a short-form invoice payable under your standard PO terms.

I attached a simple schedule showing the math and suggested invoice wording. If you want a smaller immediate payment and the rest amortized into the renewal, we can model that as well.

Let us know which path Alcove prefers and we’ll route the DocuSign or updated invoice.

— Ben Carter
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: proposed_credit_schedule.pdf)

Ben / Avery —

Thanks — we appreciate the quick turnaround and the goodwill credit. Alcove accepts the proposed net one-time top-up of $7,950 and the 90-day burst concession. A couple of small asks:

- Can Redwood mark the adjusted invoice (ALC-3342) as "one-time staging reconciliation" in the invoice description so our AP team can match it to the PO?
- Please include a short note in the DocuSign that confirms the $4,500 goodwill credit is non-recurring and does not change committed capacity numbers for the renewal.

We’ll route the invoice to purchasing for immediate payment once we receive it. Also looping in our CFO (purchasing@alcove.com) who will sign the DocuSign when it arrives.

If possible we’d like the adjusted invoice and DocuSign sent by EOD Tuesday so the renewal conversation can proceed without a billing blocker.

Appreciate your help.

— Sofia Ramos
Director, Platform Engineering
Alcove Systems
